title: Head shape may be encoded in time-dependent rather than steady voltage patterns

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Head shape may be encoded in time-dependent rather than steady voltage patterns

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because single-image voltage distributions showed no simple correspondence with the head shapes of octanol-treated G. dorotocephala, the authors consider it most likely that shape outcomes are encoded in time-dependent bioelectric activity rather than in steady voltage distributions, as in information encoding in the central nervous system.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The most likely explanation however is that shape outcomes may not be encoded via steady (single-image) distributions but in time-dependent activity, as occurs during information encoding in the central nervous system.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.4. Bioelectric State of Tissues and Its Stable Alteration in Species-Specific Shape Change”. Scope: Planarian bioelectric patterns and head-shape outcomes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-15: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The hypothesis has a clear predictive test, but the required voltage movies paired with later morphology were identified as missing. Static images cannot adjudicate a claim specifically about temporal encoding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Acquire cell-resolved voltage movies through regeneration and test whether temporal features predict final head class better out of sample than static voltage maps. Failure of temporal models to outperform static and non-bioelectric predictors would refute the proposal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Longitudinal voltage imaging in living planaria is technically difficult.

The paper explicitly reports no cell-resolution spatiotemporal voltage dataset.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.8
data existence: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A head-to-head comparison of snapshot versus time-varying voltage features would decide the encoding claim. The paper reports single images and the absence of a simple correspondence, and it does not deposit movies. That comparison therefore waits on new or newly released time-resolved recordings.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Predict head class from single-time voltage images and from time-resolved voltage features in the same animals. Higher out-of-sample accuracy for the time-resolved features would support time-dependent encoding; equal or better accuracy from the snapshots would refute that preference.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Several non-voltage gap-junction signals remain compatible with a failed snapshot correlation.

No public time series of planarian voltage paired with later head shape exists for this protocol.
